title: Psalm 74:1–23
context: A Maskil of Asaph. The sanctuary is smashed: why cast off forever? Enemies roar in the meeting place, hack carved work, burn the dwelling, and burn every meeting place of God in the land. No signs, no prophet. Yet God is King from of old who split sea and crushed Leviathan; he is asked to remember the covenant, not forget the life of the poor, and rise against foolish taunt.

voices.heading: Voices from both camps
voices.intro: Arminian and Reformed writers of the past on the ruined sanctuary, God as King from of old who crushed the sea-monsters, and the plea to remember the covenant, in their own words.
voices.note: Quotations lightly abridged for length; wording follows standard English translations of the sources named.

arminian.quote: Smoke—That is, be angry. Sheep—whom thou wast wont to guard and feed as a shepherd. Remember—consider thy relation to them. Heritage—whom thou didst choose and set apart for thyself. Rod—the tribe of Judah, from which the sceptre was not to depart. Purchased—by a mighty hand. Congregation—the people of Israel. Mount Zion—the place of thy special presence. Lift up—destroy them, as men lift up an ax to hew down trees. Carved work—the beautiful works and ornaments of the temple. Sanctuaries—the temple and synagogues. Signs—tokens of God’s presence. Prophet—to tell us how long. How long—shall this desolation continue. King—thou hast been our King, and wilt be so still. Divided—by thy power. Dragons—large fishes or crocodiles. Leviathan—the whale or some other great fish. Meat—to be food for the people of Israel. Day—the sun. Night—the moon and stars. Covenant—made with Abraham. Dark places—of the land, where the enemies exercised their cruelty. Fool—who though he pretend to be wise, yet in truth is a fool. Cause—plead for us. Arise—exert thy power. Foolish—impious and blasphemous.
arminian.source: Explanatory Notes upon the Old Testament (on Ps 74)

reformed.quote: The faithful complain that God has cast off his people, that the sanctuary is defiled and burned, that no signs or prophets remain… Yet they recall that God is their King of old, who divided the sea, broke the heads of the dragons, and gave Leviathan for meat… They plead the covenant, the oppression of the poor, and the reproach of the foolish enemy, praying that God would arise and plead his own cause. In extreme desolation faith still argues from God’s former works and from his covenant faithfulness, not from the people’s merit.

verses.text: God, why have you rejected us forever? Why does your anger smolder against the sheep of your pasture?
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: Smoke—be angry; Sheep—whom thou wast wont to guard. Forever and smoking anger feel total.

The question is prayer, not atheism. Sheep still address the Shepherd; grace invites the why without licensing despair’s final word.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: faithful complain God has cast off his people—anger like smoke against the flock. The forever is the wound’s language.

Cast-off dread is brought to God. Sheep of pasture remain covenant identity under wrath’s feel.

verses.text: Remember your congregation, which you purchased of old, which you have redeemed to be the tribe of your inheritance: Mount Zion, in which you have lived.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: Remember relation; Heritage—chosen; Purchased by mighty hand; Mount Zion—special presence.

Purchase, redeem, heritage, Zion—history is the plea. God is asked to remember what he did, while the people still cry remember.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: remember the congregation purchased of old, redeemed as heritage, Zion where he dwelt. Covenant memory is faith’s argument.

Purchase and dwelling are God’s acts; merit is not the ground.

verses.text: Lift up your feet to the perpetual ruins, all the evil that the enemy has done in the sanctuary.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: lift/steps toward perpetual ruins; enemy destroyed all in the sanctuary.

Ruins are ‘perpetual’ to the eye—prayer asks God to walk the wreck. Shared seriousness about sacred space violated.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: perpetual desolations—the enemy has done in the sanctuary. God is begged to inspect the ruin.

Sanctuary wreck is not minimized.

verses.text: Your adversaries have roared in the middle of your assembly. They have set up their standards as signs.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: foes roar in the meeting place; set their signs for signs—pagan markers replace God’s.

Sacrilege is loud. Roaring in God’s assembly is blasphemy both camps name as such.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: enemies roar in the assemblies; set up their ensigns for signs—profane triumph inside holy space.

Shared outrage at signs displacing God’s.

verses.text: They behaved like men wielding axes, cutting through a thicket of trees.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: Lift up—destroy as men lift ax to hew trees. Temple beauty treated as timber.

Violence is workmanlike and pitiless. Carved worship space meets lumberjacks.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: ax-men in a thicket—systematic hacking of holy woodwork.

Destruction is deliberate craft of hate.

verses.text: Now they break all its carved work down with hatchet and hammers.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: Carved work—beautiful ornaments of the temple—broken with hatchets and hammers.

Art offered to God is smashed. Shared grief—beauty dedicated is not spared by the foe.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: carved work broken down—nothing ornate left. Desecration completes robbery.

Hammers preach contempt for God’s house.

verses.text: They have burned your sanctuary to the ground. They have profaned the dwelling place of your Name.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: sanctuary fired; dwelling of the Name profaned to the ground.

Name’s dwelling burned—shared horror. Prayer after arson still addresses the Name.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: sanctuary set on fire; dwelling place of the name cast to the ground. Profanation is total in appearance.

Fire against the Name’s house is assault on God.

verses.text: They said in their heart, “We will crush them completely.” They have burned up all the places in the land where God was worshiped.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: Sanctuaries—temple and synagogues burned across the land. Utter subdue is the foe’s intent.

Every meeting place of God in the land was targeted. Corporate worship’s erasure is the enemy’s strategy.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: burn all meeting places of God in the land—sweeping policy against worship.

Subdue-them ideology meets the God who still hears.

verses.text: We see no miraculous signs. There is no longer any prophet, neither is there among us anyone who knows how long.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: Signs—tokens of presence; Prophet—to tell how long; How long—desolation’s duration unknown.

Absence of sign and prophet is confessed honestly. Agreed: not knowing how long still leaves room to ask the King of v. 12.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: no signs; no prophet; none knows how long. Extreme desolation includes prophetic silence.

Silence is part of the trial; faith will argue from old works next.

verses.text: How long, God, shall the adversary reproach? Shall the enemy blaspheme your name forever?
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: How long shall desolation and scoff continue? Name reviled forever is intolerable.

How-long prayer resists forever-scoff. God’s name, not only Israel’s comfort, is at stake.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: how long shall the adversary reproach and blaspheme the name forever? The cause is God’s honor.

Scoff against the Name fuels intercession.

verses.text: Why do you draw back your hand, even your right hand? Take it from your chest and consume them!
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: why is the right hand withheld, kept in the bosom—power unused to the eye.

Bold complaint asks for action. Grace allows why without dethroning God.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: why withdraw the hand—keep the right hand in the bosom? Faith pleads for the arm once known in Exodus deeds.

Anthropomorphism of withheld hand is prayer, not dogma that God cannot act.

verses.text: Yet God is my King of old, working salvation throughout the earth.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: King—thou hast been our King and wilt be; from of old, working salvation mid-earth.

Yet turns the psalm. Shared confession—God is King from of old; salvation history is the ground of fresh asking.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: yet God is my King of old, working salvation throughout the earth. Memory of kingship steadies complaint.

Yet God is the hinge; not yet we.

verses.text: You divided the sea by your strength. You broke the heads of the sea monsters in the waters.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: Divided by power; Dragons—large fishes/crocodiles—heads broken.

Exodus might recalled. Creation-combat and Red Sea memory underwrite hope in ruin.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: divided the sea; broke dragons’ heads on the waters—former salvation works.

Might once shown is argued back to God.

verses.text: You broke the heads of Leviathan in pieces. You gave him as food to people and desert creatures.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: Leviathan—whale or great fish; Meat—food (for desert scavengers / people in the figure).

Crushed chaos-monster becomes food—total victory image. God, not Israel, crushed Leviathan.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: Leviathan’s heads broken; given for meat in the wilderness—triumph complete.

Shared mythic-scale victory language for the King’s past acts.

verses.text: You opened up spring and stream. You dried up mighty rivers.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: springs opened; ever-flowing streams dried—water mastery both ways.

God commands water for salvation purposes (rock-streams; Jordan/Reed Sea).
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: cleave fountain and flood; dry up mighty rivers—sovereign hydrography of redemption.

Creation’s water answers its King.

verses.text: The day is yours, the night is also yours. You have prepared the light and the sun.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: Day—the sun; Night—moon and stars established. Time itself is God’s.

Day and night ownership rebukes the foe’s ‘forever’ scoff.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: day and night are his; he prepared light and sun. Cosmic order is covenant God’s.

Lights established by the same King who owns Zion’s ruin prayer.

verses.text: You have set all the boundaries of the earth. You have made summer and winter.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: boundaries fixed; summer and winter made. Seasons and borders are gifts.

Shared providence—geography and calendar confess the Creator while temples burn.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: set all borders of earth; made summer and winter—fixed orders.

Ruin of sanctuary does not unmake the Maker of seasons.

verses.text: Remember this, that the enemy has mocked you, LORD. Foolish people have blasphemed your name.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: Fool—pretends wisdom, is fool; Name reviled. Remember the scoff.

Foolish people = blasphemers. Remember is plea for God’s honor.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: remember the enemy’s reproach; foolish people blaspheme the name. Argument from God’s glory.

Folly of reviling the Name.

verses.text: Don’t deliver the soul of your dove to wild beasts. Don’t forget the life of your poor forever.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: dove imagery—fragile congregation; poor’s life not forgotten forever.

Dove and poor need delivering remembrance. Shared tenderness—God’s poor are not beast-food by decree of the enemy.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: deliver not the soul of thy turtledove; forget not the life of thy poor forever. Tender names in hard prayer.

Israel, God’s dove and his poor, is under threat.

verses.text: Honor your covenant, for haunts of violence fill the dark places of the earth.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: Covenant with Abraham; Dark places—cruelty’s dens across the land.

Covenant regard is the ask. Both hear: violence’s habitations do not erase the covenant; they occasion pleading it.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: have respect unto the covenant—dark places full of violence’s habitations. Faith argues covenant, not merit.

Covenant is the legal mercy ground in desolation.
verses.keyContrast: Both plead the covenant amid land-wide violence. Arminians press that covenant mercy must still be sought in prayer; Reformed Christians typically stress that regard for the covenant rests on God’s faithfulness, not the people’s desert.

verses.text: Don’t let the oppressed return ashamed. Let the poor and needy praise your name.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: downtrodden not turned back ashamed; poor and needy praising the Name—outcome desired.

Shame reversed into praise. Both see: poor praise is the public answer to violence.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: oppressed not return ashamed; poor and needy praise the name—doxology from the rescued.

Shared telos—Name praised by the needy.

verses.text: Arise, God! Plead your own cause. Remember how the foolish man mocks you all day.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: Arise—exert power; Cause—plead for us; Foolish—impious blasphemy all day.

Arise and defend your cause—God’s cause and the people’s overlap.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: arise, plead thine own cause; remember foolish reproach all day. God is asked to vindicate himself.

Thine own cause centers the plea beyond private revenge.

verses.text: Don’t forget the voice of your adversaries. The tumult of those who rise up against you ascends continually.
verses.arminianNotes:
Wesley: continual uproar of foes rising against God—do not forget the noise.

Clamor goes up continually; prayer asks God not to ignore it. Undisputed: enemies against God, not only against Asaph.
verses.reformedNotes:
Calvin: forget not the voice of adversaries; tumult of those who rise against God ascends continually. Closing pressure on divine remembrance.

Continual uproar meets the King from of old (v. 12).
